resposta:
A cryptoperiod é o período de tempo durante o qual um determinado conjunto de chaves é considerado seguras para uso em sistemas criptográficos. É uma parte importante do ciclo de vida das chaves criptográficas, que inclui a geração, distribuição, armazenamento, rotação e exclusão de chaves.

Fontes:

[1] NIST SP 800-57r5: Part 3, Application-Specific Key Management Guidance, is intended to address the key-management issues associated with currently available implementations that use cryptography. [1]

[2] Applying Cryptography - Aumasson, Jean-Philippe (2018;2016), No Starch Press, Incorporated, ISBN 9781593278267: The cryptographic life cycle is the ongoing process of identifying your cryptography needs, selecting the right algorithms, provisioning the needed capabilities and services, and managing keys. Eventually, you determine that your cryptosystem is approaching the end of its shelf life and you start the cycle all over again. [2]

[3] Serious Cryptography: A practical introduction to modern cryptography - Aumasson, Jean-Philippe (2018;2016), No Starch Press, Incorporated, ISBN 9781593278267: With the exception of the one-time pad, all cryptographic systems have a limited life span. This means that, eventually, processors will reach the amount of strength required to simply guess the encryption keys used for a communication. Security professionals must keep this cryptographic life cycle in mind when selecting an encryption algorithm and have appropriate governance controls in place to ensure that the algorithms, protocols, and key lengths selected are sufficient to preserve the integrity of a cryptosystem for however long it is necessary to keep the information it is protecting secret. [3]
